notes: Event windows are hand-curated comparison windows, not detected crash dates.
Market statistics and Core Index readings are joined by the live service from the macro artifact.
Genesis has no market price; the first Blockchain.com observation is 2010-08-18.

events.name: Genesis Block
events.summary: The Bitcoin network's first block is mined. Market pricing does not begin until July 2010, so the window is an origin marker rather than an investable drawdown.
events.context: A cypherpunk proof-of-work experiment becomes a live ledger. There is no exchange tape, no Core Index equity proxy input and no tradable price at the genesis date.

events.name: Mt. Gox Collapse
events.summary: The largest early Bitcoin exchange halts withdrawals in February 2014 and files for bankruptcy, exposing custody and counterparty risk at the centre of the market.
events.context: The first institutional-scale Bitcoin failure. It followed the 2013 mania top and pushed the asset into a multi-year repair phase.

events.name: ICO Bubble Peak
events.summary: Initial coin offerings and retail speculation drive Bitcoin to its then-all-time high. The window is a peak snapshot, not a complete crash.
events.context: A token-issuance mania that pulled crypto away from its cypherpunk roots. The following winter is tracked as a separate event.

events.name: Crypto Winter
events.summary: The post-ICO unwind: Bitcoin falls from its 2017 peak through a year-long repricing as leverage, token supply and retail demand reverse.
events.context: A slow, intermarket bear market rather than a single-day liquidity shock. It is the cleanest test of whether a macro composite can distinguish a grind from a panic.

events.name: COVID-19 Shock
events.summary: The fastest global risk-off liquidation in the modern record. Bitcoin, equities, gold and Treasuries were all caught in the dash for cash before policy support stabilized markets.
events.context: A cross-asset liquidity event. The comparison is useful because the traditional 60/40 and the digital asset traded the same shock with different liquidity and duration.

events.name: Terra-LUNA Collapse
events.summary: The algorithmic stablecoin UST loses its peg and the LUNA token collapses, transmitting a solvency shock through crypto credit and lending venues.
events.context: A crypto-native bank run. It arrived after the 2021 liquidity cycle and preceded the 2022 centralized-lender failures.

events.name: Spot ETF Peak
events.summary: The post-approval institutional bid reaches its cycle peak as spot Bitcoin ETF flows, basis trades and treasury-company demand mature.
events.context: The first fully ETF-mediated Bitcoin cycle. It tests whether the macro regime signal still travels through an institutional wrapper.
